Dhammānuloma (1), Dukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (2) 2.5. Ganthagocchaka
Section on Analysis:
Root Condition.
Dependent upon a phenomenon that is a tie, a phenomenon that is a tie arises by way of the root condition: namely, the bodily tie of adherence to rules and observances.

Dependent on covetousness as a bodily tie, there is the bodily tie of adherence to rules and observances; dependent on the bodily tie of adherence to rules and observances, there is the bodily tie of insistence that "this alone is the truth.

Dependent on the bodily tie of insistence that "this alone is the truth," there is the bodily tie of covetousness; dependent on the bodily tie of covetousness, there is the bodily tie of insistence that "this alone is the truth."

Dependent on a bound phenomenon (*gantha-dhamma*), a non-bound phenomenon (*nogantha-dhamma*) arises by way of root condition (*hetu-paccaya*): dependent on the bonds, the associated aggregates and mind-produced matter arise.
Dependent on a bound phenomenon, both bound and non-bound phenomena arise by way of root condition:

dependent on the bodily bond of adherence to rites and rituals (*sīlabbata-parāmāsa-kāyagantha*), the bodily bond of covetousness (*abhijjhā-kāyagantha*), the associated aggregates, and mind-produced matter arise. (The cycle.)
Dependent on a state that is not bound (nogantha), a state that is not bound arises by way of root condition (hetupaccaya):

dependent on one aggregate that is not bound, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise … two aggregates … at the moment of rebirth-linking … dependent on the aggregates, the physical basis (vatthu) arises;
dependent on the physical basis, the aggregates arise; one great primary element … and so forth.
Dependent on a state that is not a tie (*nogantha*), a state that is a tie arises by way of root condition: dependent on aggregates that are not ties, the ties [arise].
Dependent on a state that is not a tie, states that are both ties and not ties arise by way of root condition:
dependent on one aggregate that is not a tie, three aggregates, the ties, and mind-originated matter arise … pe … dependent on two aggregates … pe ….

Dependent on both fettered and non-fettered states, a fettered state arises by way of root condition: dependent on the bodily tie of adherence to rules and observances and its associated aggregates, the bodily tie of covetousness arises. (The cycle.
Dependent on both fettered and non-fettered states, a non-fettered state arises by way of root condition:
dependent on one non-fettered aggregate and the fetters, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise … [and so on] … two [aggregates].
Dependent on the aggregates … [and so on] … and the knots (*gantha*), and dependent on the associated aggregates, mind-produced matter arises.
Dependent on a state that is both a knot and not a knot, states that are both a knot and not a knot arise by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*):

dependent on one non-knot aggregate and the bodily knot of adherence to rules and observances (*sīlabbataparāmāsa-kāyagantha*), the three [other] aggregates and the bodily knot of covetousness (*abhijjhā-kāyagantha*) arise.
And mind-originated matter …pe… and two aggregates …pe….
By way of object condition …pe… by way of non-disappearance condition.
Section on Enumeration.

In the pure (suddha) relation of cause, there are nine; in the object relation, nine; in the predominance relation, nine (nine in all cases); in the resultant relation, one; in the nutriment relation, nine ... pe ... in the non-disappearance relation, nine. This is the Positive (Anuloma).
2.5.1.1.2. Section on the Analysis of the Negative Condition (Paccayapaccanīya Vibhaṅgavāra):
Not-root (Nahetu)
Dependent on a non-fettered state, a non-fettered state arises by way of not-root condition:

dependent on one rootless non-fettered aggregate, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise … two aggregates … [and so on] … at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking (up to the non-percipient beings), and the aggregates associated with doubt and the aggregates associated with restlessness.
Dependent on [the four ties], arises delusion accompanied by doubt and accompanied by restlessness.
Dependent on a tied phenomenon, a non-tied phenomenon arises by way of not-object condition: dependent on the ties, mind-produced matter arises.

Dependent on a state that is not a tie (*nogantha*), a state that is not a tie arises by way of the condition of object (*na-ārammaṇa-paccaya*): dependent on the aggregates that are not ties, mind-produced matter arises; at the moment of rebirth-linking …pe… (up to non-percipient beings).

Dependent on a state that is both a tie and not a tie, a state that is not a tie arises by way of the condition of object: dependent on the aggregates that are ties and their associated [states], mind-produced matter arises. (Abbreviated.)
With not-predominance condition: nine; with not-proximity condition: three; with not-contiguity condition: three; with not-mutuality condition: three; with not-strong-dependence condition: three.

Regarding the section on not-prenascence, etc.: Dependent on a state that is a tie, there arises a state that is a tie by way of not-prenascence condition—namely, the adherence to the view "this is the truth" in the formless realm.

Dependent on the bodily tie of covetousness, there is the bodily tie of ill will; dependent on the bodily tie of ill will, there is the bodily tie of adherence to "this is the truth" (in the formless realm, there is no adherence to rules and observances; thus nine questions are to be formulated).
Nine [questions] regarding postnascence, nine regarding repetition, three regarding kamma, nine regarding result, one regarding nutriment, one regarding faculty.
With jhāna: one; with path: one; with association: three; with dissociation: nine; with absence: three; with disappearance: three.
Chapter on Enumeration: Pure.
One by way of non-root; three by way of non-object; nine by way of non-predominance; three by way of non-proximity; three by way of non-contiguity;
three by way of non-mutuality; three by way of non-strong-dependence; nine by way of non-prenascence; nine by way of non-postnascence; nine by way of non-repetition;
three by way of non-kamma; nine by way of non-resultant; one by way of non-nutriment; one by way of non-faculty; one by way of non-jhāna; [none] by way of non-path.
One [condition] with respect to root; three with respect to association; nine with respect to dissociation; three with respect to absence; three with respect to disappearance. 2.5.1.1.3.

Positive-Negative Conditions (Paccayānulomapaccanīya) With root condition, there are three [results] with respect to non-object; nine with respect to non-predominance. (Abbreviated; it should be counted in this manner.)

2.5.1.1.4. Positive Order of the Negative Condition (Paccayapaccanīyānuloma) With the non-root condition (nahetupaccaya), there is one [condition] in the object condition (ārammaṇa) … pe … one in the proximity condition (anantara) … pe … one in the non-disappearance condition (avigata). 2.5.1.2.
Chapter on Co-nascence (Sahajātavāra)
The section on co-nascence is similar to the section on dependence. 2.5.1.3.
The Section on Conditions (Paccayavāra). 2.5.1.3.1.
Positive Conditions (Paccayānuloma).
Vibhaṅgavāra: Root Condition.
Conditioned by a state that is a tie, a state that is a tie arises by way of root condition... three. (The same as in the Paṭiccavāra.)
Conditioned by a state that is not a fetter (nogantha), a state that is not a fetter arises by way of root-condition (hetupaccaya):

conditioned by one aggregate that is not a fetter, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise … pe … [conditioned by] two aggregates … pe … at the moment of rebirth-linking … pe … conditioned by the aggregates, the physical basis (vatthu) arises;
conditioned by the physical basis, the aggregates arise. One great primary element … pe … the physical basis … pe … [conditioned by the physical basis, the aggregates arise].

Conditioned by states not associated with the ties (*nogantha*), aggregates arise that are not associated with the ties. Conditioned by a state not associated with the ties, a state associated with the ties arises by way of root condition: conditioned by aggregates not associated with the ties, the ties arise; conditioned by the [heart-]base, the ties arise.

Conditioned by a state not associated with the ties, states both associated with the ties and not associated with the ties arise by way of root condition: [conditioned by] a state not associated with the ties...

Conditioned by one aggregate that is a tie (*gantha*), there arise three aggregates that are ties and mind-produced matter … [and so on] … conditioned by two aggregates … [and so on] … conditioned by the physical basis (*vatthu*), there arise the ties and the associated aggregates.
Conditioned by a state that is both a tie and not a tie, a state that is a tie arises by way of root condition (*hetupaccaya*): namely, adherence to rules and observances (*sīlabbataparāmāsa*).

With the body-tie and the associated aggregates as conditions, the body-tie of covetousness [arises] (the cycle). With the adherence to rules and observances, the body-tie, and the physical basis as conditions, the body-tie of covetousness [arises] (the cycle).
With a phenomenon that is both a tie and not a tie as condition, a phenomenon that is not a tie arises by way of root-condition—[namely,] a phenomenon that is not a tie...

Conditioned by one aggregate that is a tie (*gantha*) and a tie itself, there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter … [and so on] … conditioned by two aggregates … [and so on] … conditioned by ties and the physical basis (*vatthu*), there arise aggregates that are not ties.
Conditioned by a state that is both a tie and not a tie, states that are both a tie and not a tie arise by way of root condition— [namely,] the state that is not a tie.

Conditioned by one aggregate, by the bodily tie of adherence to rules and observances, and by the bodily tie of covetousness, there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter … two aggregates … (The cycle.
Conditioned by the bodily tie of adherence to rules and observances, by the [heart-]base, and by the bodily tie of covetousness, there arise the associated aggregates. (The cycle.)
In the Pure Conditioned-By-Cause Enumeration:
nine in the object condition, nine in the predominance condition …pe… nine in the non-disappearance condition.
Positive Order.
2.5.1.3.2. Negative Analysis of Conditions: Section on Exposition.
Conditioned by a non-fettered state, a non-fettered state arises by way of not-root condition:

conditioned by one rootless non-fettered aggregate, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise … two aggregates … [and so on] … at the moment of rebirth-linking … [up to] non-percipient beings … conditioned by the eye-base, eye-consciousness arises … [and so on].
Conditioned by the body-base, there arises body-consciousness. Conditioned by the [heart-]base, there arise rootless aggregates not associated with the ties;
and conditioned by both the doubt-accompanied or restlessness-accompanied aggregates and the base, there arises doubt-accompanied or restlessness-accompanied delusion. (Abbreviated.
Section on Enumeration.
Pure:
one by way of not-root condition, three by way of not-object condition, nine by way of not-predominance condition. (Enumerate in this manner. 2.5.1.3.3.
Positive-Negative Conditions (Paccayānulomapaccanīya)
With root condition, there are three [answers] for non-object; nine for non-predominance …pe… three for non-disappearance.
2.5.1.3.4. Positive-Negative Conditions:
With non-root condition, there is one [answer] for object …pe… one for non-disappearance.

2.5.1.7. Section on Questions (Pañhāvāra)
2.5.1.7.1. Positive Order of Conditions (Paccayānuloma):
Analysis Section (Vibhaṅgavāra) – Root Condition (Hetu)

A bound phenomenon (gantha-dhamma) is a condition for a bound phenomenon by way of the root-condition (hetu-paccaya): bound roots are a condition for associated bound phenomena by way of the root-condition.
A bound phenomenon is a condition for an unbound phenomenon by way of the root-condition: bound roots are a condition for associated aggregates and mind-produced matter by way of the root-condition.

A tied phenomenon (gantha-dhamma) is a condition, by way of root-condition (hetu-paccaya), for both a tied phenomenon and an untied phenomenon: the roots that are tied are a root-condition for their associated aggregates, for the tied [phenomena], and for mind-produced matter.

An untied phenomenon is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an untied phenomenon: the roots that are untied are a root-condition for their associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter; at the moment of rebirth-linking ... pe ... [end].
A non-fettered state is a condition for a fettered state by way of root-condition: non-fettered roots are a condition for associated fetters by way of root-condition.
A non-fettered state is a condition for both a fettered and a non-fettered state by way of root-condition:
non-fettered roots are a condition for associated aggregates, for fetters, and for mind-produced matter by way of root-condition.

States that are both fetters and not-fetters are related to a state that is a fetter by way of root-condition: roots that are both fetters and not-fetters are related to associated fetters by way of root-condition.

States that are both fetters and not-fetters are related to a state that is not a fetter by way of root-condition: roots that are both fetters and not-fetters are related to associated aggregates and mind-produced matter by way of root-condition.
Fetters and non-fetters as phenomena are related to fettered and non-fettered phenomena by way of the root condition:
roots that are both fetters and non-fetters are related to their associated aggregates and to the mind-produced matter by way of the root condition.
A bound phenomenon (*gantha-dhamma*) is related to a bound phenomenon by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*): taking the bonds as object, the bonds arise.
(The root should be formulated. Taking the bonds as object, non-bound aggregates (*nogantha-khandhā*) arise. (The root...)
(To be done. Taking books as the object, both the books and the associated aggregates arise.
A non-book phenomenon is a condition for a non-book phenomenon by way of the object-condition (ārammaṇapaccaya): having given a gift, [observed] virtue...
pe ...having performed the Uposatha duty, one reviews it; [one reviews] past well-performed deeds... pe ...jhānas... pe ...the Noble Ones [review their attainments].
Having emerged from the path, they review the path, review the fruit, and review Nibbāna.
Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage, purification, the path, the fruit, and adverting by way of object-condition.
Noble ones review the defilements abandoned [by the path], …pe… the defilements suppressed, and the past...
... [and so on] ... the eye ... [and so on] ... the physical basis, one contemplates the non-bondage aggregates as impermanent ...

[and so on] ... and grief arises; one sees a form with the divine eye, hears a sound with the divine ear-element. By means of the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, one knows the mind of one possessing a mind not bound [to oneself];
the base of infinite space [is related] to the base of infinite consciousness ... [and so on] ... the base of nothingness [is related] to the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
... pe ... the visible-form base is a condition for eye-consciousness ... pe ... the tangible-object base is a condition for body-consciousness ... pe ...

the unobstructed aggregates are a condition, by way of object-condition, for the knowledge of supernormal powers, the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings according to their karma, the knowledge of future states, and for advertence.
A state that is not a tie (*gantha*) is a condition, by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*), for a state that is a tie: having given a gift, observed virtue ... [etc] ...
performed the Uposatha duty, one relishes it and delights in it; taking that as an object, lust arises, wrong view arises, and grief arises.
[Or: formerly well-practiced deeds ... [etc] ... jhānas ... [etc] ... the eye ... [etc] ... the physical basis (*vatthu*).
One relishes and delights in the non-fettered aggregates; taking them as an object, lust arises … [and so on] … grief arises.
A non-fettered state is a condition for both fettered and non-fettered states by way of object-condition:
having given a gift, observed virtue … [and so on] … performed the Uposatha duty, one relishes and delights in it; taking that as an object, the fetters arise.
The aggregates associated with the ties arise; previously well-practiced [virtues] … pe … jhānas … pe … the eye … pe … one relishes and delights in the basis and the aggregates that are not tied;
conditioned by that, the ties and the associated aggregates arise.
Bonds and non-bonds are related to a bond-dharma by way of the object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*) … three. (These are to be formulated starting from "taking as an object.
Predominance:

A bond-dharma is related to a bond-dharma by way of the predominance-condition (*adhipatipaccaya*) … three. (These are similar to the object-conditions; they are to be formulated with weighty objects.)
A non-obstructed state is a condition for a non-obstructed state by way of predominance-condition:
as object-predominance and as conascence-predominance. Object-predominance: [taking as object] generosity ... morality ... the observance-day rite ... former [meritorious deeds] ...
jhānas ... noble paths ... fruits ... Nibbāna ... Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage (gotrabhū).
[It is] a condition for purification, the path, and the fruit by way of predominance-condition (*adhipatipaccaya*). The eye ... [and so on] ... the physical basis (*vatthu*);
one esteems, relishes, and delights in the non-associated aggregates (*khandha*), and by esteeming them, lust arises and wrong view arises.
Co-nascent predominance (*sahajātādhipati*): non-associated predominance is a condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter.

Material phenomena are related to material phenomena by way of predominance condition. A non-fettered state is related to a fettered state by way of predominance condition: as object-predominance and as conascence-predominance. Object-predominance:
[taking] giving … precept … the observance-day rite … previously well-performed deeds … jhānas … [as objects].
... pe ... [regarding] the eye ... pe ... [regarding] the basis, one esteems, relishes, and delights in the non-fettered aggregates;
esteeming that, lust arises and wrong view arises. Conascent predominance: non-fettered predominance is a condition for the fetters by way of the predominance condition.
A non-fettered state is a condition for both a fettered and a non-fettered state by way of predominance-condition:
as object-predominance and as conascence-predominance. Object-predominance: [Regarding] a gift ... [etc. ...
one esteems, relishes, and delights in non-fettered aggregates; esteeming them, both fetters and the associated aggregates arise. Conascence-predominance: Non-fettered predominance.
The associated aggregates and the fetters are a condition for mind-produced matter by way of the predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*).
Fetters and states that are not fetters are a condition for a state that is a fetter by way of the predominance condition: (1) object-predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*) ... [three].
Immediate (*anantara*)...

A bound phenomenon (*gantha-dhamma*) is a condition for a bound phenomenon by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*): preceding bound phenomena are a condition for succeeding bound phenomena by way of proximity-condition.
A bound phenomenon is a condition for an unbound phenomenon (*nogantha-dhamma*) by way of proximity-condition:
preceding bound phenomena are a condition for succeeding unbound aggregates (*khandha*) by way of proximity-condition; [as are] the bound...
It is a condition for emergence by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).
A tied state (*gantha-dhamma*) is a condition for both a tied state and a non-tied state by way of proximity-condition:
preceding tied states are a condition for succeeding tied states and their associated aggregates (*khandha*) by way of proximity-condition.
A non-fettered state is a condition for a non-fettered state by way of proximity-condition … three. (Two applications of mind should be performed; the first does not exist.
Fettered and non-fettered states are conditions for a fettered state by way of proximity-condition … three. (One emergence should also be performed in the middle.
Immediately-sequential, etc.

A state that is a tie is related to a state that is a tie by way of the condition of immediate succession: nine [ways]. … By way of the condition of co-nascence: nine. … By way of the condition of mutuality: nine. … By way of the condition of support:
nine. Strong-dependence:
A state that is a tie is related to a state that is a tie by way of the condition of strong-dependence—namely, object-strong-dependence (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*).
Proximity-strong-dependence, natural strong-dependence … [as above] … Natural strong-dependence: books are related to books by way of strong-dependence condition … three.
A state that is not a tie (nogantha) is related to a state that is not a tie by way of strong-dependence condition:
object-strong-dependence, proximity-strong-dependence, natural strong-dependence … [as above] … Natural strong-dependence: relying on faith, one gives a gift.
...gives a gift ... pe ... arouses conceit, adopts a view; relying on virtue ... pe ... a lodging, one gives a gift ... pe ... causes a schism in the Saṅgha; faith ... pe ...
a lodging is a strong-support condition for faith ... pe ... for the attainment of fruition by way of the strong-support condition.
A state that is not a tie is a strong-support condition for a state that is a tie: by way of object-strong-support, [and] natural strong-support.
Proximity-strong-dependence, natural strong-dependence … [and so on] … Natural strong-dependence: relying on faith, one adopts wrong view;
[relying on] virtue … [and so on] … relying on a lodging, one kills a living being … [and so on] … one causes a schism in the Saṅgha.
Faith … [and so on] … a lodging is a condition for lust … [and so on] … for aspiration by way of the condition of strong-dependence.
A non-fettered state is a condition for both a fettered and a non-fettered state by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*)—
namely, as object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, and natural decisive support … [as follows] … Natural decisive support:
relying on faith, one arouses conceit, adopts wrong view, [or develops] virtue … [and so on] … Relying on a lodging, one kills a living being … [and so on] … [one harms] the Saṅgha.
Confidence … [and so on] … lodging-place is related to the ties and to the aggregates associated with them by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

Ties and states that are not ties are related to a state that is a tie by way of decisive support condition—namely, object-decisive support (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*), proximity-decisive support (*anantarūpanissaya*), and natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*) … [and so on] … Natural decisive support … three [cases]. (These should be formulated according to the method of the object.)
A non-clinging state that is pre-arisen, etc., is a condition for a non-clinging state by way of the pre-arisen condition—namely, object-pre-arising and base-pre-arising. Object-pre-arising:
the eye …pe… [regarding] the base as impermanent …pe… [giving rise to] grief.

[It] arises; one sees a form with the divine eye, hears a sound with the divine ear-element, the base of visible forms for eye-consciousness … [and so on] … the base of tangible objects for body-consciousness … [and so on] …. Base-prenascence:
the eye-base for eye-consciousness … [and so on] … the body-base for body-consciousness … [and so on] … the physical basis for the non-clinging aggregates.
Conditioned by the relation of prenascence.
A non-tied state is related to a tied state by the relation of prenascence: namely, object-prenascence and base-prenascence.
Object-prenascence: the eye ... [as above] ... one relishes and delights in the base; that [is related to the tied states].
Taking [these] as a basis, lust arises, wrong view arises, and displeasure arises. Object-prenascence:
the physical basis is a condition for the fetters by way of the prenascence condition.
A state that is not a fetter is a condition for a state that is both a fetter and not a fetter by way of the prenascence condition—namely, object-prenascence.
Base-prenascence. Object-prenascence: the eye ... [as above] ... one relishes and delights in the base;
conditioned by that, the fetters and the associated aggregates arise. Base-prenascence: the base is a condition, by way of prenascence-condition, for the fetters and the associated aggregates.
Conditioned by post-nascence condition ... three; conditioned by repetition condition ... nine.
Kamma:
A non-fettered state is a condition for a non-fettered state by way of kamma condition—conascent and asynchronous.
Co-nascent: volition that is not a fetter is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for the associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter;
at the moment of rebirth-linking … [etc. … Asynchronous: volition that is not a fetter is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for resultant aggregates and for kamma-born matter.
A non-fettering state is a condition for a fettering state by way of kamma-condition: non-fettering volition is a condition for the associated fetters by way of kamma-condition.
A non-fettering state is a condition for both a fettering and a non-fettering state by way of kamma-condition:
non-fettering volition is a condition for the associated aggregates, for the fetters, and for mind-produced matter by way of kamma-condition.
A non-fettered state that is resultant, etc., is a condition for a non-fettered state by way of the resultant condition … one; by way of the nutriment condition … three;
by way of the faculty condition … three; by way of the jhāna condition … three.
… a condition by way of path-condition … nine … a condition by way of association-condition … nine.
Dissociation:
A tied-up state is a condition, by way of dissociation-condition, for a state that is not tied up—conascent, postnascent. (Abbreviated.)
A state that is not a tie (*nogaṇtha*) is a condition for a state that is not a tie by way of dissociation-condition (*vippayutta-paccaya*): conascent, prenascence, and postnascence. (Abbreviated.

A state that is not a tie is a condition for a state that is a tie by way of dissociation-condition. Prenascence: the physical basis (*vatthu*) is a condition for the ties by way of dissociation-condition.

A state that is not a tie is a condition for a state that is both a tie and not a tie by way of dissociation-condition. Prenascence: the physical basis is a condition for the ties and for the associated aggregates (*khandha*) by way of dissociation-condition.
Both fettered and non-fettered states are related to a non-fettered state by way of dissociation condition: conascent and postnascent. (Abbreviated.
There is a case where a fettered state is related to a fettered state by way of presence condition: one. (As in the Paṭicca [Dependent] chapter.)
Fetters are related to states that are not fetters by way of presence condition—namely, by way of conascence and postnascence. As conascence:
fetters are related to their associated aggregates and to mind-produced matter by way of presence condition.
As postnascence: fetters are related to this prenascent body by way of presence condition.
A tied-up state is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for both a tied-up state and an untied-up state … one. (The same as in the Paṭicca-vibhaṅga.
An untied-up state is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for an untied-up state: conascent, prenascence, postnascence, nutriment, faculty. (Abbreviated.
An untied-up state is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for a tied-up state: conascent, prenascence.
Co-nascent: non-fettered aggregates are a condition for the fetters by way of presence-condition (*atthipaccaya*).
Pre-nascent: the eye … [and so on] … the physical basis (*vatthu*); one relishes and delights in it; taking that as object, lust arises, wrong view arises, and grief arises.
The physical basis is a condition for the fetters by way of presence-condition.
A non-fettered state is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for both a fettered state and a non-fettered state: namely, conascence and prenascence. By way of conascence:
one conascent non-fettered aggregate is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for three aggregates that are fetters and for mind-produced matter … (as appropriate) … By way of prenascence:
the eye … (as appropriate) … [or] the [heart-]base is enjoyed and relished; [thus it is a condition].
Taking that as object, the fetters and the associated aggregates arise; the physical basis is a condition for the fetters and the associated aggregates by way of presence-condition (*atthipaccaya*).
Fetters and phenomena that are neither fetters are conditions for a fetter-phenomenon by way of presence-condition—namely, conascence (*sahajāta*).

Pre-arisen [condition]. Co-nascent: the bodily tie of adherence to rules and observances and its associated aggregates are related to the bodily tie of covetousness by way of presence condition (*atthipaccaya*) (the cycle).

A cause (hetu) that is both a tie (gantha) and associated with ties, and a state associated with ties, are conditions by way of root-condition (hetupaccaya) for a state that is both a tie and associated with ties:
namely, roots that are both ties and associated with ties are [root-conditions] for the associated ties.
Condition by way of root-condition:
A state that is both a tie and associated with ties is related to a state that is associated with ties but is not itself a tie,
by way of root-condition— the roots that are both ties and associated with ties are related to their associated aggregates.
Conditioned by way of root-condition:
A state that is both a tie (gantha) and associated with ties is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is both a tie and associated with ties,
and for a state that is associated with ties but is not itself a tie— that is, [the states] which are both ties and associated with ties.
And roots that are associated with the fetters (gantha) are a condition by way of root-condition for the aggregates and the fetters that are associated with them.
A state that is both associated with the fetters and is not itself a fetter is a condition by way of root-condition for a state that is both associated with the fetters and is not itself a fetter:
namely, roots that are associated with the fetters and are not themselves fetters [are a condition] for the [associated] aggregates.
The fetters are related to the fetters by way of root condition.
A state that is both associated with the fetters and not itself a fetter is related to a state that is both a fetter and associated with the fetters by way of root condition:
roots that are both associated with the fetters and not themselves fetters are related to the associated fetters by way of root condition.
Conditioned by way of root-condition:

A state that is both associated with the ties and not itself a tie is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is both a tie and associated with the ties, for a state that is associated with the ties but not itself a tie,
and for a state that is both associated with the ties and not itself a tie— [namely,] those states associated with the ties but not themselves...
And the fetters are a condition, by way of root-condition, for the aggregates associated with the fetters and for the fetters themselves.
Phenomena that are both fetters and associated with fetters, as well as phenomena that are associated with fetters but are not fetters, are a condition, by way of root-condition,
for a phenomenon that is both a fetter and associated with fetters— that is, for those [phenomena] which are both fetters and associated with fetters.
And the roots that are both associated with the fetters and not themselves fetters are related to their associated aggregates by way of root-condition.

Phenomena that are both fetters and associated with fetters, as well as phenomena that are associated with fetters but are not themselves fetters, are related to a phenomenon that is associated with fetters but is not itself a fetter by way of root-condition—the fetters that are both fetters and associated with fetters... And roots that are both associated with the fetters and not themselves fetters are related to their associated aggregates by way of root-condition.
Phenomena that are both fetters and associated with the fetters, as well as phenomena that are associated with the fetters but are not themselves fetters,
are related to a phenomenon that is both a fetter and associated with the fetters, as well as to a phenomenon that is associated with the fetters but is not itself a fetter.

Condition by way of root-condition: roots that are both fetters and associated with fetters, as well as roots that are associated with fetters but are not themselves fetters, are a condition by way of root-condition for their associated aggregates and for the fetters. taking the aggregates that are both associated with the fetters and not themselves fetters as object.
Aggregates associated with the fetters (*gantha*) but not themselves fetters arise. (The root should be formulated.
Taking aggregates associated with the fetters but not themselves fetters as object, the fetters arise. (The root should be formulated.
Taking aggregates associated with the fetters but not themselves fetters as object, both the fetters and the aggregates associated with the fetters arise.

nine by way of co-nascence (sahajāta), nine by way of mutuality (aññamañña), nine by way of dependence (nissaya), nine by way of decisive support (upanissaya), nine by way of repetition (āsevana), three by way of kamma (kamma), [three] by way of nutriment (āhāra)...
Three [ways] for faculty, three for jhāna, three for path, nine for association, nine for presence, nine for absence, nine for disappearance, and nine for non-disappearance.
